passage:
Keiko: Serious runners never walk during a race. You push through or you don't bother.
Sam: My sister walked through a few water stations at the Brackwater Marathon and still finished under four hours.
Keiko: Then with respect, she's not a serious runner.
cue: Then with respect, she's not a serious runner.
explanation: When Sam offers a counterexample, Keiko doesn't revise her claim; she declares Sam's sister not a "serious runner," using the very walking break in question as the reason.

whyNot.fal_special_pleading: Keiko isn't exempting anyone from a rule; she redefines who counts as a serious runner so the counterexample no longer counts.

passage: Every week someone says I'm wrong about this, so let's settle it: homemade bread stays fresh for a full week on the counter. Yes, Marco, I saw your comment about your loaf going stale in two days. Respectfully, if it went stale that fast, it wasn't real homemade bread.
cue: if it went stale that fast, it wasn't real homemade bread
explanation: Marco's loaf is a counterexample to Hollie's claim. Instead of revising the claim, she rules his loaf "not real" homemade bread, and her only reason is that it went stale.

whyNot.fal_moving_the_goalposts: Hollie isn't demanding more proof from Marco; she redefines "homemade bread" so his loaf no longer counts.

title: Re: Q3 delivery review
passage: Hi Omar, thanks for pulling the delivery numbers together; that's really useful. On the Harbor project slipping three weeks: I'd gently push back on reading that as a knock on the framework. Teams that genuinely run our sprint process don't miss dates like that, so if Harbor slipped, they weren't truly running it. Happy to talk Thursday. Bettina
cue: if Harbor slipped, they weren't truly running it
explanation: Harbor is a counterexample: a team that used the process and still slipped. Bettina decides it wasn't "truly" using the process, judged only by the fact that it slipped.

whyNot.fal_special_pleading: Bettina isn't exempting the framework from a rule; she redefines who counts as using it so the miss can't count against it.

source: Nutrition coach Imogen Hale · Wexbridge community health fair
passage: Great question. You're saying your father has eaten fish, olive oil and vegetables every day for decades and still has high cholesterol. I'd say that tells us he isn't truly eating the Mediterranean way, because people who genuinely follow it don't end up with high cholesterol. That's how powerful this diet is.
cue: he isn't truly eating the Mediterranean way, because people who genuinely follow it don't end up with high cholesterol
explanation: The father matches every usual description of the diet. Imogen rules him out as not "truly" following it only because his cholesterol is high, which shields her claim from any counterexample.

whyNot.fal_moving_the_goalposts: Imogen isn't raising a bar for evidence; she redefines who counts as following the diet so the counterexample disappears.

title: Sturdy, quiet, and worth learning to use
passage: Sturdy frame, quiet motor, and the memory presets are handy. I've noticed a few one-star reviews from people whose back pain got worse after switching. With respect, that just means they weren't using it correctly. Anyone who uses a standing desk the right way ends up with a healthier back; that's the whole point of them.
cue: that just means they weren't using it correctly
explanation: Paolo dismisses reviewers whose pain got worse by saying they used the desk wrong, but his only sign of wrong use is the pain itself. No reviewer could ever count against his claim.

whyNot.fal_special_pleading: Paolo isn't exempting himself or the desk from a rule; he defines "correct use" so any counterexample is excluded automatically.

source: Director Felicity Amadi · Quillfield Learning Center parent night
passage: That's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it in front of everyone. Yes, a student from last spring's group scored 1150 after attending every session. But our results speak for themselves: students who fully commit to our program score above 1300. If she didn't get there, she wasn't fully committed, whatever her attendance sheet says.
cue: If she didn't get there, she wasn't fully committed, whatever her attendance sheet says
explanation: Felicity faces a student who did everything and scored 1150. Rather than soften her claim, she declares the student not "fully committed," with the low score as the only evidence.

whyNot.fal_moving_the_goalposts: Felicity isn't raising the bar for proof in a debate; she redefines who counts as a committed student so the 1150 can't count.

title: Delicious, but please fix the label
passage: The texture is great and the frosting isn't too sweet. But the "vegan" label needs to go: the ingredient card at the counter lists butter and honey. Vegan means no animal products, and both of those come from animals, so this cupcake doesn't qualify, however tasty it is. Please relabel it for those of us who check.
cue: Vegan means no animal products, and both of those come from animals
explanation: Tamar excludes the cupcake using the standard, agreed definition of vegan and the listed ingredients, not a definition invented to dodge a counterexample.

whyNot.fal_no_true_scotsman: The definition Tamar applies existed beforehand and is widely shared, so excluding the cupcake isn't an after-the-fact redefinition.

title: Gullhaven marathon course found 2.1 miles short
passage: A certified remeasurement found that Sunday's route was only 24.1 miles. Because a marathon is defined as 26.2 miles, race officials say finish times can't be listed as marathon results or used to qualify for other races, though every finisher will still receive a medal.
cue: Because a marathon is defined as 26.2 miles
explanation: Officials say the race didn't count as a marathon because it failed a fixed, official distance confirmed by a certified measurement, not because of an awkward result.

whyNot.fal_no_true_scotsman: The 26.2-mile standard was set long before the race, so excluding the results applies a prior definition rather than inventing one.
